Subject: Liminal MAP — cutover windows + canary questions

Olga / Redwood team —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Leadership is aligned and legal signed the SOW. Before we lock dates with engineering, a couple quick asks to make sure our internal teams are prepared: 

- Can you share a single-sheet MAP that embeds the post-signature implementation milestones (rollout phases, canary, migration, training)?
- We need two proposed canary windows (low-traffic and high-traffic) and a short checklist for each (what success looks like, rollback criteria).
- Any constraints on data migration that will require scheduled downtime / freeze windows?

Goal: target production cutover in Q4 but flexible on exact week — want to confirm resource commitment and training calendar first.

Thanks —
Samir Rao
VP Product, Liminal Health
samir@liminalhealth.com

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Samir Rao <samir@liminalhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-18T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Liminal MAP — cutover windows + canary questions

Samir —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a working MAP (Liminal_MAP_v1.xlsx) that embeds the post-signature implementation plan. High-level notes below and a link to the live doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAP_Liminal

High-level approach (embedded in the MAP sheet):

1) Phase 0 — Prep (weeks 0–2): account provisioning, access lists, test data snapshot, canary cluster prep.
2) Phase 1 — Internal canary (week 3): low-traffic canary with feature flags and KV cache warming. Success = no more than 2% error increase, stable latency SLA.
3) Phase 2 — Staged migration (weeks 4–6): migrating non-critical routes, runbook rehearsals, training ops and CS.
4) Phase 3 — External canary (week 7): broader traffic slice (10–20%), validate cost/latency at scale, evaluation plan attached (see 'canary-checklist.pdf').
5) Phase 4 — Full cutover & hypercare (week 8): scheduled cutover, immediate rollback window (2 hours), 72-hour elevated support.

Notes on data migration / downtime:
- We recommend online incremental migration for embeddings and token caches; full read-only freeze only for final snapshot (target 30–60 minutes).
- If Liminal requires stricter windows, we can plan the freeze for weekend nights — please advise preferred windows.

Training plan (summary):
- 2 instructor-led sessions for DevOps and CS pre-canary; recorded playbacks for product teams.
- Runbook walkthrough + tabletop exercises during Phase 1.

Attachments: Liminal_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + timeline) and canary-checklist.pdf (detailed gating criteria and rollback steps).

Next steps / asks for you:
- Confirm preferred weekend freeze window or call out blackout dates.
- Approve provisional canary weeks (we tentatively propose internal canary the week of Oct 12; external canary the week of Oct 26).

I'll loop in Ben for capacity sizing and Rishi for the rollback policy.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-09-19T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Liminal MAP — cutover windows + canary questions

Quick technical notes from infra/capacity side —

- Canary sizing: for internal canary we recommend 2x expected baseline concurrent requests per instance to exercise autoscale; for external canary size to 25% of projected production TPS.
- Autoscaling policy: configure aggressive scale-up with a 20s evaluation window and conservative scale-down (10m) during canary to avoid oscillation.
- Capacity reservation: we can reserve burst nodes for the final cutover (estimated 3 x p3-standard equivalents) for the 8-hour window — will need approval from Liminal to bill as reserved capacity (or we can run as on-demand, but cost will be higher).

Rollback triggers (high level):
- Error rate > 5% sustained for 10 minutes.
- Latency P95 increase of >200ms compared to baseline.
- Cache miss rate doubling causing downstream throttles.

I'll add these to the MAP sheet and the canary checklist. Olga, I'll flag the reserved capacity numbers in the document and mark them as 'requires procurement sign-off'.

-Ben
Ben Carter

Thanks — adding training specifics here so the MAP has an operational training track: 

Training schedule (proposed):
- Week 2 (pre-canary): 90-minute runbook and playbook session for Liminal DevOps + CS engineers (live).
- Week 3 (pre-canary rehearsal): tabletop incident simulation (60 minutes) with Redwood and Liminal ops.
- Week 6 (pre-external canary): 60-minute session focused on monitoring dashboards, alerting thresholds, and on-call handoffs.
- Post-cutover (week 9): 45-minute lessons-learned + knowledge transfer with recordings and runbook updates.

Deliverables: slide deck, recording, runbook PDF, incident simulation notes. We will attach slide deck v1 to the MAP folder once finalized.
